outcome_detail: On October 4, 2022, a federal jury in the U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado (Whitson v. Hanna, No. 1:18-cv-02076) awarded $8.25 million against former Sheriff Thomas Hanna personally: $3.25 million compensatory and $5 million punitive damages. The district court had dismissed the Monell claims against Sedgwick County, but on July 5, 2024 the Tenth Circuit (No. 23-1084) reversed, holding the county could be liable because Hanna acted as final policymaker for the custody and care of prisoners. On December 20, 2024, Sedgwick County reportedly agreed to pay $2.7 million to settle the revived claims against the county.
criminal_detail: Hanna was criminally charged with sexual assault on an at-risk adult, sexual misconduct in a correctional setting, kidnapping, and soliciting prostitution. In May 2018 a Logan County jury convicted him only of misdemeanor first-degree official misconduct (for transporting the detainee in his personal vehicle to his home) and acquitted him of the sexual-assault and other felony charges. He was sentenced to seven months in jail with work release as a condition of 12 months of probation, and lost his Colorado peace officer certification. He had been removed from office by recall election in 2017.
description: A developmentally disabled woman held in the Sedgwick County jail sued former Sheriff Thomas Hanna and Sedgwick County under 42 U.S.C. Section 1983, through her guardian ad litem, in Colorado federal court in 2018. According to the complaint, in August 2016 Hanna transported the woman toward the Logan County jail in his personal pickup truck in violation of policy, but instead drove her to his home, offered her money for sex, and, when she refused, sexually assaulted her and threatened consequences if she disclosed it. In October 2022 a federal jury found Hanna liable for excessive force, cruel and unusual punishment, and false imprisonment, awarding $8.25 million including $5 million in punitive damages. In a criminal trial, a jury acquitted Hanna of sexual assault charges but convicted him of misdemeanor official misconduct, for which he served a seven-month jail sentence. In July 2024 the Tenth Circuit reinstated the claims against Sedgwick County, and the county reportedly settled for $2.7 million in December 2024.
notes: Filed before 2021; included because resolution occurred in window (2022 verdict; 2024 appellate ruling and county settlement). Settlement fields record the county's separate $2.7M settlement, which is in addition to (not part of) the $8.25M jury verdict against Hanna personally.
